proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\partial}
 =\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}
   (d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)
\]
for the subfamily in the statement.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}nonempty}\) shows that, under the supplied labeled order and queried-edge conditions, this class is nonempty exactly when
\[
 \kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}.
\]
Thus the regular stratum is not merely formal in that feasible range.  If the inequality fails, the subfamily is empty and the uniform assertion is vacuous.  Below \(d,m,G,\mathcal Z,\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa\) are fixed, \(\mathcal Z\) is finite and nonempty, and \(n\to\infty\); all suprema are over \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}\).  The fine-parameter set underlying \(\mathfrak P_{\partial}\) is compact: the zero restrictions and the two separation inequalities define closed subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space, while the entry and innovation bounds make the set bounded; the innovation lower bound makes \(D\) positive definite.  For every such \((A,D)\), the stability margin gives a unique stationary Gaussian law, so it is enough below to take subsequences in this compact \((A,D)\)-parameter set.

Let
\[
 \vartheta=\operatorname{vec}_{s}(M_0,M_1),
 \qquad
 \widehat\vartheta=\operatorname{vec}_{s}(\widehat M_0,\widehat M_1),
 \qquad
 \rho=1-\gamma.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}coarse\mbox{-}law\mbox{-}reduction}\), the observed process has the innovation representation
\[
 Y_s=BY_{s-1}+\eta_s,
 \qquad
 B=A^m,
 \qquad
 \eta_s\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}\sigma(Y_{s-1},Y_{s-2},\ldots),
 \qquad
 \eta_s\sim N(0,Q),
\]
and
\[
 B=M_1M_0^{-1},
 \qquad
 Q=M_0-BM_0B^\top.
\]
The positivity assumptions contained in \(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}class}\) imply
\[
 Q=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top\succeq D\succeq d_{\min}I_d
\]
and, by stationarity,
\[
 M_0=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^kQ(B^k)^\top
     =\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}A^rD(A^r)^\top
     \succeq Q\succeq d_{\min}I_d.                                      \tag{1}
\]
There is also a uniform finite upper bound.  Indeed, lower triangularity, the entry envelope, and \(|A_{ii}|\le\rho<1\) imply, by expanding powers along nondecreasing vertex walks, that a constant \(C_A<\infty\), depending only on \(d,L,\rho\), satisfies
\[
 \lVert A^r\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_A(r+1)^{d-1}\rho^{(r-d+1)_+},
 \qquad r\ge0.
\]
There are at most \(d-1\) strict increases in such a walk; choosing their locations gives the polynomial factor, while every remaining step is diagonal and contributes at most \(\rho\).  Hence the innovation upper bound gives
\[
 M_0\preceq
 d_{\max}\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}\lVert A^r\rVert_{
 \mathrm{op}}^2 I_d
 \preceq C_0I_d                                                     \tag{2}
\]
for a finite constant \(C_0=C_0(d,L,\gamma,d_{\max})\).  Equations \((1)\) and \((2)\) state explicitly that inversion of \(M_0\) is uniformly legitimate.  Consequently the map
\[
 (M_0,M_1)\longmapsto
 \bigl(B,Q\bigr)
 =\bigl(M_1M_0^{-1},,M_0-M_1M_0^{-1}M_1^\top\bigr)                 \tag{3}
\]
is twice continuously differentiable, with uniformly bounded first and second derivatives, on a common neighborhood of the population moment set.

We next analyze the graph-recursive inverse.  For a diagonal coordinate, \(B_{ii}=A_{ii}^m\), and the derivative-separated definition gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial B_{ii}}{\partial A_{ii}}\right|
 =m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}\ge\kappa.                                        \tag{4}
\]
Because \(m\) is odd, the real diagonal root is unique.  Equation \((4)\) and the inverse-function calculation show that its first derivative has magnitude at most \(\kappa^{-1}\); its second derivative is uniformly bounded because \((4)\) also keeps \(|A_{ii}|\) uniformly away from zero.  For every allowed off-diagonal coordinate, \(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}class}\) gives
\[
 |C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})|\ge\kappa.                                    \tag{5}
\]
The recursion in \(\mathrm{thm{:}odd\mbox{-}regular\mbox{-}identification}\) is
\[
 A_{ij}=\frac{B_{ij}-R_{ij,m}(A)}{C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})}.               \tag{6}
\]
At endpoint gap \(i-j\), the polynomial \(R_{ij,m}\) in \((6)\) contains only coordinates recovered at smaller endpoint gaps.  Starting with the diagonal roots and inducting over the finitely many endpoint gaps, equations \((5)\) and \((6)\) therefore express every recovered coordinate as a twice continuously differentiable function of \(B\).  Compactness of the coefficient set and continuity of the finitely many denominators imply that a common moment neighborhood keeps the absolute values in \((4)\) and \((5)\) at least \(\kappa/2\).  On that neighborhood, the first and second derivatives of the entire root recursion are uniformly bounded.  The innovation recursion is also smooth because its denominators obey
\[
 \sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_{ii}^{2r}\ge1,                                  \tag{7}
\]
although the queried transfer depends only on the recovered matrix \(A\).

For \(z\in\mathcal Z\subset\mathbb T\), the stability boundary is separated uniformly:
\[
 |1-A_{vv}z|\ge1-|A_{vv}|\ge\gamma.                                \tag{8}
\]
Thus the coefficient-to-transfer map is twice continuously differentiable on the same common neighborhood.  Direct differentiation gives
\[
 \mathrm dh_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{z}{1-A_{vv}z}\,\mathrm dA_{vu}
  +\frac{A_{vu}z^2}{(1-A_{vv}z)^2}\,\mathrm dA_{vv}.               \tag{9}
\]
Let \(F(\vartheta)\) stack the real and imaginary parts of \((h_{uv}(z))_{z\in\mathcal Z}\), and let \(J_h(\vartheta)\) be the Jacobian of the composite of \((3)\), the recursion \((4)\)--\((7)\), and \((9)\).  The preceding uniform second-derivative bounds give, whenever \(\widehat\vartheta\) is in the common neighborhood,
\[
 F(\widehat\vartheta)-F(\vartheta)
 =J_h(\vartheta)(\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta)+r_n,
 \qquad
 \lVert r_n\rVert
 \le C\lVert\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta\rVert^2.                 \tag{10}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}lag\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}clt}\) implies both uniform tightness of \(\sqrt n(\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta)\) and
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta)
 \Longrightarrow N(0,\Omega(P))                                   \tag{11}
\]
uniformly in \(P\).  Therefore the neighborhood event in \((10)\) has probability tending to one uniformly, and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 P\{\sqrt n\lVert r_n\rVert>\epsilon\}\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(\epsilon>0).                                               \tag{12}
\]
Combining \((10)\)--\((12)\) proves the asserted uniform Gaussian limit
\[
 \sqrt n\{F(\widehat\vartheta)-F(\vartheta)\}
 \Longrightarrow N(0,\Sigma_h(P)),
 \qquad
 \Sigma_h(P)=J_h(\vartheta)\Omega(P)J_h(\vartheta)^\top.           \tag{13}
\]

The covariance series in the lag-moment central limit lemma converges absolutely and uniformly, and every summand is a continuous Gaussian Isserlis polynomial in the coarse covariance sequence.  Hence \(P\mapsto\Omega(P)\), and therefore \(P\mapsto\Sigma_h(P)\), is continuous.  Let \(\widetilde\Omega\) be the Isserlis plug-in estimator supplied by that lemma, let \(\widehat\Omega\) be its projection onto the positive-semidefinite cone, and compute \(\widehat J_h\) by the same recursion at the empirical moments.  The stability margin for \(B=A^m\), consistency of \(\widehat B\), and continuity of spectral radius imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}P\{\widehat B\text{ is not stable}\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
The central limit lemma consequently gives \(\widehat\Omega-\Omega(P)=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly; positive-semidefinite projection cannot increase Frobenius distance to the positive-semidefinite target.  Equations \((4)\)--\((10)\) also give \(\widehat J_h-J_h=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly.  It follows that
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_h
 =\widehat J_h\widehat\Omega\widehat J_h^\top
 =\Sigma_h(P)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)                                    \tag{14}
\]
uniformly, and \(\widehat\Sigma_h\) is positive semidefinite by construction.

It remains to treat rank and the random critical value.  Define the conventional lagged denominator
\[
 \widetilde M_0=n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n}Y_{s-1}Y_{s-1}^\top.
\]
The empirical-moment definition gives the exact boundary identity
\[
 \widehat M_0-\widetilde M_0
 =n^{-1}(Y_nY_n^\top-Y_0Y_0^\top).                                 \tag{15}
\]
The uniform covariance bound \((2)\) makes the right side of \((15)\) equal to \(o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  Using the coarse innovation equation and \((1)\), expansion of \(\widehat B=\widehat M_1\widehat M_0^{-1}\) yields
\[
 \sqrt n\,\operatorname{vec}(\widehat B-B)
 =\operatorname{vec}\!\left{
 n^{-1/2}\sum_{s=1}^{n}\eta_sY_{s-1}^\top M_0^{-1}
 \right}+o_{\mathbb P}(1).                                       \tag{16}
\]
The summands in \((16)\) are martingale differences.  Independence of \(\eta_s\) from the past gives their covariance, up to the fixed vectorization convention, as
\[
 \Gamma_B=M_0^{-1}\otimes Q.
\]
By \((1)\), \((2)\), and \(Q\succeq d_{\min}I_d\),
\[
 \Gamma_B\succeq c_BI_{d^2},
 \qquad c_B=\frac{d_{\min}}{C_0}>0.                                \tag{17}
\]

Because \(u\to v\in G\), equation \((6)\) recovers \(A_{vu}\) as an allowed coordinate, and its remainder involves only smaller gaps.  Thus
\[
 \frac{\partial A_{vu}}{\partial B_{vu}}
 =\frac{1}{C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})},
 \qquad
 \frac{\partial A_{vv}}{\partial B_{vu}}=0.                        \tag{18}
\]
Furthermore, \(|A_{ii}|\le\rho<1\) gives
\[
 |C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})|
 \le\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}|A_{vv}|^r|A_{uu}|^{m-1-r}
 \le m,
 \qquad
 |1-A_{vv}z|\le1+|A_{vv}|\le2.                                   \tag{19}
\]
Combining \((9)\), \((18)\), and \((19)\), the derivative in the real direction \(B_{vu}\) satisfies
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial h_{uv}(z)}{\partial B_{vu}}\right|
 =\frac{1}{|C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})|\,|1-A_{vv}z|}
 \ge\frac{1}{2m}.                                                  \tag{20}
\]
Equations \((17)\) and \((20)\) show that, for the limiting complex coordinate \(Z_h(z)\),
\[
 \mathbb E|Z_h(z)|^2\ge\frac{c_B}{4m^2}>0                          \tag{21}
\]
uniformly for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\).  Hence the limiting vector is never identically zero, although \(\Sigma_h(P)\) may be singular because different frequencies can be linearly dependent.

For a real vector written in complex-coordinate pairs, define
\[
 \lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal Z,\infty}
 =\max_{z\in\mathcal Z}\sqrt{x_{\Re,z}^2+x_{\Im,z}^2}.
\]
For a positive-semidefinite matrix \(\Sigma\), let \(Z_\Sigma\sim N(0,\Sigma)\), and let
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma)
 =\inf\{t:\Pr(\lVert Z_\Sigma\rVert_{\mathcal Z,\infty}\le t)
                  \ge1-\alpha\}.                                  \tag{22}
\]
The parameter set is compact, the covariance series is continuous, and \((21)\) bounds the covariance family away from the zero matrix.  On the support subspace of any nonzero centered Gaussian vector, the Gaussian law has a positive density and \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal Z,\infty}\) is a norm.  Every norm sphere has Lebesgue measure zero in that subspace, while every nonempty norm annulus has positive measure.  Therefore the distribution in \((22)\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \((0,\infty)\), with no atom at zero.  If \(\Sigma_j\to\Sigma\), continuity of the positive-semidefinite square root gives \(Z_{\Sigma_j}\Rightarrow Z_\Sigma\); the preceding strict continuity then gives
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma_j)\longrightarrow c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma).
\]
Thus the quantile map is continuous on the compact covariance family.  Equation \((14)\) consequently implies
\[
 \widehat c_{1-\alpha}
 =c_{1-\alpha}(\widehat\Sigma_h)
 =c_{1-\alpha}(\Sigma_h(P))+o_{\mathbb P}(1)                       \tag{23}
\]
uniformly.

Finally, suppose uniform coverage failed.  Then there would be a sequence \(P_n\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}\) along which the coverage error stayed bounded away from zero.  Compactness supplies a subsequence on which the fine parameters, and hence \(\Sigma_h(P_n)\), converge.  The uniform limit \((13)\), the critical-value convergence \((23)\), and the absence of mass at the limiting boundary imply along that subsequence
\[
 \Pr_{P_n}\!\left{
 \max_{z\in\mathcal Z}\sqrt n\,
 |\widehat h_{uv}(z)-h_{uv}(z)|
 \le\widehat c_{1-\alpha}
 \right}\longrightarrow1-\alpha,                                 \tag{24}
\]
a contradiction.  The event in \((24)\) is exactly the simultaneous event
\[
 h_{uv}(z)\in
 \left\{w\in\mathbb C:
 |w-\widehat h_{uv}(z)|\le\frac{\widehat c_{1-\alpha}}{\sqrt n}
 \right\}
 \quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal Z.
\]
This proves the stated uniform Wald coverage, including at coefficient values with \(A_{vu}=0\) and at covariance matrices that are rank deficient across frequencies.

added_lemmas.statement:
If every arrow \(j\to i\) in \(G\) satisfies \(j<i\) and \(u\to v\in G\), then the derivative-separated regular class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\) is nonempty if and only if
\[
 \kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(\rho=1-\gamma\).  If the class is nonempty, its defining derivative separation and the stability-margin condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}class}\) give, for every \(i\in V\),
\[
 \kappa\le m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}\le m\rho^{m-1}.
\]
This proves necessity.

Conversely, suppose \(\kappa\le m\rho^{m-1}\), and define
\[
 a=\left(\frac{\kappa}{m}\right)^{1/(m-1)},
 \qquad
 \delta=\frac{d_{\min}+d_{\max}}{2},
 \qquad
 A=aI_d,
 \qquad
 D=\delta I_d.
\]
Because \(\kappa>0\), \(m\) is odd on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\), and \(m\ge2\), the number \(a\) is well defined and satisfies \(0<a\le\rho<1\).  The matrix \(A\) is lower triangular and obeys every graph-support zero restriction.  It also satisfies \(\max_{ij}|A_{ij}|=a<1\le L\).  The matrix \(D\) is diagonal and satisfies
\[
 d_{\min}I_d\preceq D\preceq d_{\max}I_d.
\]
For every allowed edge \(j\to i\),
\[
 C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})=C_m(a,a)
 =\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}a^{m-1}
 =ma^{m-1}=\kappa,
\]
and, for every \(i\), \(m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}=\kappa\).  Let \((\varepsilon_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) be independent \(N(0,D)\) vectors and set
\[
 X_t=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}a^r\varepsilon_{t-r},
 \qquad Y_s=X_{ms}.
\]
The series converges in \(L^2\), since \(a^2<1\), and it is the stationary Gaussian solution of \(X_t=AX_{t-1}+\varepsilon_t\).  Thus every condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}class}\), as well as the additional derivative separation in \(\mathrm{def{:}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}regular\mbox{-}class}\), holds.  This proves sufficiency.

proposed.name: derivative-separated regular odd-factor class
proposed.construction:
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\) is the set of all \((A,D,(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z},(Y_s)_{s\in\mathbb Z};d,m,G)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\) such that
\[
 \min_{i\in V}m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}\ge \kappa.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires the diagonal-root derivative-separated regular subfamily to be an explicit documented object rather than an unnamed restriction inside the Wald theorem.

proposed.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal Z\ne\varnothing\), \(u\to v\in G\), and restrict \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\) further by \(\min_{i\in V}m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}\ge\kappa\). Uniformly over this subfamily, \(\sqrt n\big((\widehat h_{uv}(z)-h_{uv}(z))_{z\in\mathcal Z}\big)\) converges to the centered Gaussian law obtained by applying the Jacobian of the moment-to-root recursion and \(\mathrm dh(z)=z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}/(1-A_{vv}z)+A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}/(1-A_{vv}z)^2\) to the long-run Gaussian lag-moment covariance. Let \(\widehat\Sigma_h\) be the positive-semidefinite plug-in estimate obtained from the Gaussian Isserlis covariance series and the recursive Jacobian, and let \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\) be the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the maximum complex modulus of the corresponding centered Gaussian vector. Then the simultaneous disks \(\{w\in\mathbb C:|w-\widehat h_{uv}(z)|\le \widehat c_{1-\alpha}/\sqrt n\}\), \(z\in\mathcal Z\), have coverage converging to \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over the subfamily.
proposed.justification: The explicitly defined derivative-separated odd stratum is feasible exactly when \(\kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}\), and on that stratum it supports familiar simultaneous uncertainty quantification without global branch inversion.
proposed.gap: Fine-grid process-graph Wald theory does not establish the uniform Jacobian and Taylor bounds created by an aliased triangular root recursion, nor the quantile argument needed when the cross-frequency Gaussian covariance changes rank.
proposed.consumer: Researchers can check the two separation margins directly, use simultaneous Wald disks when they hold, and revert to the exact branch-free inverse confidence set otherwise.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof now uses the explicit derivative-separated class, its nonvacuity certificate, and the established coarse-law reduction; these proof-spine dependencies must be recorded.

prose_updates.tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, so causal identification depends on the complete root-and-innovation fiber rather than on a selected numerical root. The paper gives parity-sharp graph recursion and exact transfer-aware algebraic certification. On the explicitly defined derivative-separated odd stratum, a uniformly valid delta method yields simultaneous Wald disks; the stratum is nonempty exactly in the feasible separation range. Globally, a finite-sample coarse-moment region is inverted through every branch, and the measurable constant-envelope fallback reproduces the deterministic moment box pathwise, preserving coverage without claiming a strict adaptive gain.

project_justification.fill: The project gives a parity-sharp graph recursion, a universal even-factor same-law obstruction, a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with exact witnesses, simultaneous Wald disks on an explicit derivative-separated odd class, and finite-sample branch-free inversion of a rationally rounded coarse-moment region. The covariance-envelope fallback is measurable and pathwise no wider because it exactly reproduces the deterministic box; it is a validity fallback, not an adaptive improvement.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \((M_0,M_1)\) by overlapping empirical lag moments. On the derivative-separated odd stratum, map them through \((\widehat B,\widehat Q)\), the graph recursion, and the rational transfer, and use the Isserlis long-run covariance with the recursive Jacobian for simultaneous Wald disks. Globally, invert the rationally outward-rounded moment box through all fine-grid branches; the constant covariance-envelope fallback is measurable and coincides pathwise with that deterministic box.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The algebraic identification and ambiguity results concern stable, ordered, finite-dimensional Gaussian VAR(1) systems with known subsampling factor, supplied labeled process DAG, and diagonal fine-grid innovation covariance. Under the supplied order and queried-edge conditions, the Wald theorem is local to the odd-factor class with both divided-difference and diagonal-root derivative separation; this class is nonempty exactly when \(\kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}\). The limiting covariance may be singular across frequencies but is uniformly nonzero in the queried-edge direction. Outside that class, inference uses branch-free inversion rather than branch selection. The constant covariance-envelope construction proves finite-sample validity and equality of widths with the deterministic box, not strict adaptive improvement. Exact CAD certifies termination rather than polynomial-time scalability, and executable witnesses require effective real-closed-field input. No claim is made about unknown causal order, unknown sampling factor, high-dimensional rates, VARMA or unit-root extensions, or the scientific validity of the Temperature--Ozone ordering.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq 3\) and a data-generating law \(P\) in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})\).  Give the trajectory space \(\Omega_n=\mathbb R^{(n+1)d}\) its Borel sigma-field and define the covariance-envelope statistic
\[
 \widehat K_{\Sigma,n}:\Omega_n\longrightarrow(0,\infty),
 \qquad \widehat K_{\Sigma,n}(w)=K_\Sigma.
\]
This map is measurable: for every Borel set \(E\subseteq(0,\infty)\), its inverse image is \(\Omega_n\) if \(K_\Sigma\in E\) and is empty otherwise.

Let \(\Sigma_{n,P}=\operatorname{Cov}_P(W_n)\).  The coarse spectral-density resolvent bound established in \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\), with the compact-class bounds from \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\), gives, for every such \(P\) and every \(n\geq3\),
\[
 0\preceq \Sigma_{n,P},
 \qquad
 \|\Sigma_{n,P}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq K_\Sigma
 =\widehat K_{\Sigma,n}(W_n)
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Thus the constant envelope dominates the trajectory covariance at finite sample size, simultaneously over the compact class, on an event of probability one.  To see explicitly that it is admissible in the spectral-split handle, let \(H_{\ell ij}^{+}\) and \(H_{\ell ij}^{-}\) be the positive and negative spectral parts prescribed by \(\mathrm{def{:}adaptive\mbox{-}calibration\mbox{-}handle}\).  For either sign \(s\in\{+,-\}\), positivity and the preceding operator bound imply
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(H_{\ell ij}^{s}\Sigma_{n,P})
 \leq K_\Sigma\operatorname{tr}(H_{\ell ij}^{s}),
 \qquad
 \bigl\|\Sigma_{n,P}^{1/2}H_{\ell ij}^{s}
              \Sigma_{n,P}^{1/2}\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K_\Sigma\|H_{\ell ij}^{s}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Indeed, the trace inequality follows from
\(0\preceq\Sigma_{n,P}\preceq K_\Sigma I\) after congruence by
\((H_{ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}\), and the operator inequality follows from
submultiplicativity of the operator norm.  Hence the positive and negative quadratic-form parts are both controlled by this measurable envelope.  Recombining them supplies the same two-sided deterministic calibration used in \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\); no data-dependent branch choice is involved.

Now define, sample by sample, the fallback regions displayed in the statement:
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)=\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal R}_n=\mathcal R_n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h=\mathcal C_n^h.
\]
For every coordinate \((\ell,i,j)\), its interval in the first set is therefore exactly
\[
 \operatorname{Out}_N\!\left((\widehat M_\ell)_{ij},
 2K_\Sigma\left\{\sqrt{\frac{\log(4d^2/\alpha)}{n}}
 +\frac{\log(4d^2/\alpha)}{n}\right\}\right),
\]
which is the corresponding interval in \(\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\) by
\(\mathrm{def{:}moment\mbox{-}box}\).  Consequently every coordinate width is equal, sample by sample, to its deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) counterpart.  In particular,
\[
 P\!\left\{\text{all fallback coordinate widths are no larger than
 their deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) counterparts}\right\}=1.
\]

Because the two moment regions are identical, the finite-sample uniform guarantee in \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\) yields
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})}
 P\!\left\{(M_0,M_1)\in
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)\right\}
 =
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})}
 P\!\left\{(M_0,M_1)\in
 \mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\right\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\]
Every endpoint is rational because it is returned by \(\operatorname{Out}_N\).  Moreover, the equalities \(\widetilde{\mathcal R}_n=\mathcal R_n\) and \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h=\mathcal C_n^h\) leave unchanged every polynomial equality, inequality, and rational endpoint in \(\mathrm{def{:}inverse\mbox{-}region}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}transfer\mbox{-}confidence\mbox{-}set}\).  Thus the exact semialgebraic encoding and its branch-free inversion are preserved.

For completeness, on the event \((M_0,M_1)\in\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)\), the stationary moment identities from \(\mathrm{lem{:}coarse\mbox{-}law\mbox{-}reduction}\), together with membership of the true model in the compact class, put its true pair \((A,D)\) in \(\widetilde{\mathcal R}_n\).  The definition of the transfer set then gives
\[
 h_{uv}(z)=\frac{A_{vu}z}{1-A_{vv}z}
 \in\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h.
\]
The denominator is nonzero for \(|z|=1\), since the compact-class stability margin gives \(|A_{vv}|\leq1-\gamma<1\).  This is also exactly the implication formalized by \(\mathrm{thm{:}global\mbox{-}honest\mbox{-}inversion}\).  Hence the fallback retains finite-sample transfer coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).  All asserted width comparisons are equalities; no strict adaptive improvement is claimed.
